questions.problem:
Let 
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}y \\ x\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

- $T(kv)=kT(v)$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vector $v$ and real scalar $k$
- $T({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})=T({v}_{1})+T({v}_{2})$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$
- $T$ is a linear transformation
questions.worked_solution:
A linear transformation $T$ satisfies two properties:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T[\begin{aligned}kx \\ ky\end{aligned}]=kT[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}], \\  & T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Checking the first condition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T[\begin{aligned}kx \\ ky\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}ky \\ kx\end{aligned}] \\  & =k[\begin{aligned}y \\ x\end{aligned}] \\  & =kT[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Checking the second condition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{T}$ is a linear transformation.

As a result, all three statements are true.

questions.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}54 \\ -36 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(21{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2}).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, since ${v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}21{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2} & =18{v}_{1}+3{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2} \\  & =18({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})+3{v}_{1} \\  & =18(0)+3{v}_{1} \\  & =3{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(21{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2})=T(3{v}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(3{v}_{1}) & =3T({v}_{1}) \\  & =3[\begin{aligned}54 \\ -36 \\ 30\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}162 \\ -108 \\ 90\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(21{v}_{1}+18{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}162 \\ -108 \\ 90\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2}).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2} & =13{v}_{1}+13{v}_{2}-5{v}_{2} \\  & =13({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})-5{v}_{2} \\  & =13(0)-5{v}_{2} \\  & =-5{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2})=T(-5{v}_{2}).
$$

 

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-5{v}_{2}) & =-5T({v}_{2}) \\  & =-5[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}40 \\ -20 \\ -45\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(13{v}_{1}+8{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}40 \\ -20 \\ -45\end{aligned}].$
